t: You're on Queen Anne's Gate, a street in Westminster lined with Grade I listed houses in the Queen Anne style. Pevsner and Bradley called the early eighteenth century houses the best of their kind in London. The street is named for Queen Anne, who reigned until 1714. Being close to Parliament, it attracted politicians. Lord Palmerston was born at number 20, and philosopher John Stuart Mill lived at number 40. Mansfield Smith-Cumming, the founder of MI6, lived at number 21, and Admiral Jacky Fisher at number 16. The architect Arthur Cawston died here in 1894.
